exact_embedding.domain: X=(1/2)D, where D is the full l1 unit diamond
exact_embedding.proof: Since D is centrally symmetric and convex, X-X=D. Conversely every h in D is realized by i=-h/2,j=h/2 in X. Thus Theorem1's inequalities for every displacement in V_X are exactly our inequalities for every full-D shift and every Borel noise event. The zero shift adds only the identity inequality. No density or radiality is inserted by this equivalence.

regularity_is_not_the_obstruction_in_thi: The constant-off-zero ell is regular under Definition3: if endpoints differ, at least one adjacent pair differs, so epsilon<=epsilon or2epsilon; if endpoints coincide, the left side is0.

actual_circularization_obstructions.Theorem5: X=(1/2)D is not a Euclidean disk
actual_circularization_obstructions.Theorems6_and7: For every d0>0 and d>0, ell(d0+d)=epsilon<2epsilon=ell(d0)+ell(d). Their required superadditivity-at-d0 condition fails. Therefore these theorems do not replace the original sensitivity diamond by a rotationally symmetric global budget.

other_prior_results: Theorem8 is an optimal-member existence statement for a specified uniformly bounded/tight class, not an explicit original finite-V value or optimizer characterization. Standard existence/pointwise-regulation arguments remain prior tools. Theorem9 uses distance-proportional ell(r)=epsilon*r, not this constant-off-zero embedding.
